candidate: vLLM Marlin GPTQ W4A16 full-vocabulary scan plus exact BF16 top-128 rerank
scope: Qwen3.5-0.8B, RTX 4060 Laptop SM89, max_num_seqs=1, greedy decode, vLLM fp8_per_block or GPTQ-Marlin W4A16 backbone

low_power_end_to_end_screen.protocol: same source, adjacent multiprocess runs, six natural prompts, one warmup and three trials, 128 generated tokens

non_comparable_prior_high_clock_baseline.reason: The current laptop was power limited to 780--975 MHz, so the low-power screen cannot establish speedup against the earlier high-clock frontier.

mtp1_screen.protocol: same candidate source in separate fresh processes, six natural prompts, one warmup and one measured trial, 64 generated tokens
mtp1_screen.reason: M=2 Marlin weight reuse is real, but it does not cover proposer, target verification, rejection, and runtime overhead; the M=2 backbone also changes numerical reductions before exact shortlist reranking.

gptq_backbone_qualification.protocol: two independent fresh-cache screens followed by two warmups and five measured trials on six natural prompts, then paired GSM8K n=512

w4_scan_only_boundary.reason: Only about 3.2% faster than BF16 shortlist reranking while substantially changing generated behavior; equal aggregate GSM8K accuracy is not sufficient evidence of preserved capability.

batch_service_frontier.protocol: one warmup and three measured trials, 64 generated tokens, forward/reverse batch order, max_num_seqs=8; stock-candidate-stock processes with a shared requested cache root and initialization excluded from service throughput
batch_service_frontier.policy: Opt-in rerank at batch 1; consider at batch 2 only when its approximate contract is acceptable; use stock GPTQ-Marlin at batch 4 and above.

strict_production_pipeline_frontier.protocol: two independent cold VLLM_CACHE_ROOT traces per implementation, frozen harness and prompt-token hashes, guarded source hashes, one warmup and three measured trials, 64 generated tokens
strict_production_pipeline_frontier.policy: Under the bounded approximate greedy quality contract, route active batch 1 and 2 to rerank; route batch 4 and 8 to stock GPTQ-Marlin. Under stock-GPTQ token identity, always route stock.

implementation_limitations: Output-head quantization and Marlin repacking now happen during weight post-processing, followed by a load-time warmup; the first request no longer performs packing.
The implementation uses vLLM production GPTQ quantization, row-packing, Marlin repacking, scale permutation and workspace APIs; it no longer imports a test helper.
The dense tied output-head weight remains resident beside the packed representation, adding about 0.14 GiB; it is required by both input embedding and BF16 shortlist reranking.
A prepacked sidecar can remove online conversion time, but removing the dense table requires a separate quantized-embedding candidate and a new quality qualification.
The top-128 contract is bounded empirical greedy-token identity, not full-logit or all-input mathematical equivalence.
The 512-case quality result supports an explicit approximate-speed mode only; broader tasks, sampling modes, concurrency and high-clock interleaving remain required before wider promotion.
decision: Expose only as an opt-in approximate low-concurrency greedy mode. Prefer it at batch 1, consider it at batch 2 when the approximate quality contract is accepted, and retain stock GPTQ-Marlin at batch 4 and above. It is not a lossless default because the larger quality screen is not token-identical. Reject MTP-1 at this deployment point.
